subject: Ancient India

questions.q:
With reference to ancient India, Gautama Buddha was generally known by which of the following epithets?
1. Nayaputta
2. Shakyamuni
3. Tathagata
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
options: None of the above are epithets of Gautama Buddha
questions.explain: The ancient texts refer to Mahavira as Nayaputta (son of Nayas). This referred to his clan of origin, which is translated in sanskrit as jnatra. Hence, point 1 is not correct.\n\nBuddha is frequently called Shakyamuni, the sage of the Shakya clan. In Buddhist texts, he is most commonly addressed as Bhagavat (often translated as Lord), and as the Tathagata, which can mean either one who has thus come or one who has thus gone.
questions.subject: Ancient India

questions.q: In which one of the following regions was Dhanyakataka, which flourished as a prominent Buddhist centre under the Mahasanghikas, located?
questions.explain: Dhanyakataka, also known as Amaravati, is located in present-day Andhra Pradesh. It was a well-known Buddhist center. Gandhara (modern-day Pakistan/Afghanistan) was another prominent Buddhist site but was famous for its Greco-Buddhist art, not for the Mahasanghikas. Kalinga (modern Odisha) is renowned for the Kalinga War and its role in Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism, while Magadha (modern Bihar) is where Buddhism originated, particularly under rulers like Ashoka. However, these regions did not host Dhanyakataka.

questions.q:
With reference to ancient India, how many of the following statements are correct?
1. The concept of Stupa is Buddhist in origin.
2. Stupa was generally a repository of relics.
3. Stupa was a votive and commemorative structure in Buddhist tradition.
questions.explain: The first two statements are correct: Stupas are indeed of Buddhist origin and serve as repositories of relics. However, not all stupas are commemorative or votive structures. Only one is incorrect because at least two of the statements are true, and All three is incorrect because not all stupas serve the commemorative role mentioned.

questions.q:
How many of the following dynasties established their kingdoms in early eighth century AD?
1. Hoysala
2. Gahadavala
3. Kakatiya
4. Yadava
questions.explain: None of these dynasties were founded in the early eighth century. The Hoysala and Kakatiya dynasties rose to prominence around the 10th century, while the Yadavas and Gahadavalas became influential later during the 12th century. Only one/two/three options are incorrect as none of these dynasties were founded in the early eighth century.

questions.q: Souls are not only the property of animal and plant life, but also of rocks, running water and many other natural objects not looked on as living by other religious sects.\nThe above statement reflects one of the core beliefs of which one of the following religious sects of ancient India?
questions.explain: Jainism holds the belief that souls (jivas) exist in all entities, animate and inanimate. Buddhism, while valuing compassion toward all beings, does not extend this belief to inanimate objects. Shaivism and Vaishnavism are sects of Hinduism that do not share this specific view about souls in non-living things.

questions.q:
According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, which of the following are correct?
1. A person could be a slave as a result of a judicial punishment.
2. If a female slave bore her master a son, she was legally free.
3. If a son born to a female slave was fathered by her master, the son was entitled to the legal status of the master's son.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is not correct: According to the Kautilya's Arthashastra, a person can primarily be enslaved by selling himself or being captured in the war.\nStatement 2 is correct: According to the Kautilya's Arthashastra, children born to slave and master when a slave gives birth to a child, both the mother and child shall be recognised as free and were no longer considered to be slaves.\nStatement 3 is correct: If a son born to a female slave was fathered by her master, the son was entitled to the legal status of the master's son.

Site of Ashoka's major rock edicts : Location in the State of

questions.q: Who among the following rulers advised his subjects through this inscription?\nWhosoever praises his religious sect or blames other sects out of excessive devotion to his own sect, with the view of glorifying his own sect, he rather injures his own sect very severely.
questions.explain: Major Rock Edict XII of Ashoka reads, Whosoever praises his religious sect or blames other sects out of excessive devotion to his own sect, with the view of glorifying his own sect, he rather injures his own sect very severely.

questions.q:
With reference to the religious history of India, consider the following statements:
1. Sthaviravadins belong to Mahayana Buddhism.
2. Lokottaravadin sect was an offshoot of Mahasanghika sect of Buddhism.
3. The deification of Buddha by Mahasanghikas fostered Mahayana Buddhism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is not correct: The first division in the Buddhist community occurred in 383 B.C. The order broke into Sthaviravada (in Pali Theravada) and the Mahasanghikas. While the Sthaviravadins were believers in the teaching of elders, and orthodox school. They did not belong to the Mahayana Buddhism.\nStatement 2 is correct: Subdivisions of the Mahasanghikas included aspects of Lokottarvadin whose philosophy was based on the concept of Lokottara Buddha or Supernatural Buddha. Hence, Lokottaravadin sect was an offshoot of Mahasanghika sect of Buddhism.\nStatement 3 is correct: Mahasanghika Paved the way for the emergence of the Mahayana sect of Buddhism during the 4th Buddhist Council. Mahayanist gave prominence to the Bodhisattva ideal. Thus, the deification of Buddha by Mahasanghikas fostered Mahayana Buddhism.

questions.q: With reference to the cultural history of India, which one of the following is the correct description of the term 'paramitas'?
options: The earliest Dharmashastra texts written in aphoristic (sutra) style
Philosophical schools that did not accept the authority of Vedas
Perfections whose attainment led to the Bodhisattva path
Powerful merchant guilds of early medieval South India
questions.explain: To achieve enlightenment and realise Nibbana, the Fourth Noble Truth, the Noble Eightfold Path, gives a Buddhist practitioner, ways to practice, and the path to follow. There also exists a parallel path that consists of perfecting certain qualities, in order for a pilgrim to become a self-Enlightened Universal Buddha. These qualities are termed as the Paramis (perfections) in the Southern traditions and the Paramitas in the Eastern and Northern traditions in the context of the Bodhisattva path.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Deification of the Buddha.
2. Treading the path of Bodhisattvas.
3. Image worship and rituals.
Which of the above is/are the feature/features of Mahayana Buddhism?
questions.explain: Mahayana is one of the two main schools of Buddhism. The term Mahayana is a Sanskrit word which literally means Great Vehicle. This school of Buddhism believes in the heavenliness of Buddha and Idol worship of Buddha and Bodhisattvas embodying Buddha Nature. It originated in northern India and Kashmir and then spread east into Central Asia, East Asia and some areas of Southeast Asia.

questions.q: In which of the following relief sculpture inscriptions is 'Ranyo Ashoka' (King Ashoka) mentioned along with the stone portrait of Ashoka?
questions.explain: Kanaganahalli, an important Buddhist site, dates from the 1st century BC to the 3rd century AD. It is the place where an ancient Buddhist Mahastupa site was found. It is a site in Karnataka with an inscription in Brahmi script reading Ranyo Ashoka (King Ashoka) and a sculpture of King Ashoka. The uniqueness of the Kanaganahalli image is that it is the only inscribed portrait of the Emperor encountered so far.

questions.q: With reference to the religious practices in India, the Sthanakvasi sect belongs to
questions.explain: Sthanakvasi is a sect of Svetambara Jainism founded by a merchant named Lavaji in 1653 AD. It believes that idol worship is not essential in the path of soul purification and attainment of Nirvana or Moksha. The sect is essentially a reformation of the one founded on teachings of Lonka, a fifteenth-century Jain reformer.

questions.q: With reference to India history, who among the following is a future Buddha, yet to come to save the world?
questions.explain: In Buddhist culture, Maitreya is a bodhisattva who will arrive on Earth in the future, and save the world, in order to attain complete awareness and educate about the pure dharma. According to the inscriptions, Maitreya will be an heir to the existing Buddha, Gautama Buddha. The prediction of the appearance of Maitreya relates to a time in the future when the dharma will have been neglected by most in the physical world.

questions.q:
With reference to the religious history of India, consider the following statements:
1. Sautrantika and Sammitiya were the sects of Jainism.
2. Sarvastivadin held that the constituents of phenomena were not wholly momentary but existed forever in a latent form.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is not correct: Sautrantika and Sammitiya are sects of Buddhism. Sautrantika school belongs to Hinayana Buddhism, which is one of the two schools of Buddhism, the other one being Mahayana.\nStatement 2 is correct: This sect of Buddhism believes that all things exist, and exist continuously, in the past and the future as well as in the present. Sarvastivada, also called Vaibhashika, a school of early Buddhism. A fundamental concept in Buddhist metaphysics is the assumption of the existence of dharmas, cosmic factors and events that combine momentarily under the influence of a person's past deeds to form a person's life flux, which he considers his personality and career.

questions.q:
With the reference to the religious history of India, consider the following statement:
1. The concept of Bodhisattva is central to the Hinayana sect of Buddhism.
2. Bodhisattva is the compassionate one on his way to enlightenment.
3. Bodhisattva delays achieving his own salvation to help all sentient beings on their path to it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is not correct: Bodhisattva is an ideal in Mahayana Buddhism, Bodhisattva is the individual who seeks enlightenment both for him or herself and for others.\nStatement 2 is correct: A Bodhisattva is literally a living being (Sattva) who aspires to be enlightened (Bodhi) and carries out altruistic practices. Compassion, an empathetic sharing of the sufferings of others, is Bodhisattva's greatest characteristic.\nStatement 3 is correct: Bodhisattva is an aspirant of Buddhahood (buddhatva) who works for the enlightenment of all sentient beings in contrast to that of one's own emancipation of the Arhat (an ideal in non- Mahayana traditions).

questions.q:
Which of the following kingdoms were associated with the life of Buddha?
1. Avanti
2. Gandhara
3. Kosala
4. Magadha
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Magadha, Kosala, Vaishali, Vajji, were the kingdoms and regions that were associated with the life of Buddha. Avanti was not directly related to the life of Buddha. Pasenadi (Prasenajit), King of Kosala, was the Buddha's contemporary and is frequently mentioned in Pali texts. Kosala and Magadha were linked through matrimonial ties. Buddha wandered through the towns and villages in the kingdoms of Kosala and Magadha teaching his philosophy. Gandhara is not directly associated with the life of Buddha. It was through the expansion of the Mauryan empire that Gandhara received much Buddhist influence, notably during the reign of Asoka.
questions.subject: Ancient India

questions.q:
Which of the following Kingdoms were associated with the life of the Buddha?
1. Avanti
2. Gandhara
3. Kosala
4. Magadha
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: According to Buddhist tradition, Siddhartha Gautama was born in Lumbini (modern-day Nepal) and grew up, the son of a king. He left his palace when he encountered the sufferings people faced. After the birth of his son, Buddha left KapilaVastu at the age of 29 and headed for Magadha in search of spiritual truth. In Magadha, he studied in the communities of two teachers, Alara Kalama and Uddaka Ramaputta. Kosala and Magadha kingdoms were associated with the life of Buddha. Buddha spent the last 20 years of his life in Kosala and the King Pasenadi, was his most devoted disciple.

questions.q: Which one of the following describes best the concept of Nirvana in Buddhism?
options: The extinction of the flame of desire
A state of bliss and rest
A mental stage beyond all comprehension
questions.explain: The Pali word Nibbana (nirvana in Sanskrit) was first used by the Buddha to describe the highest state of profound well-being a human is capable of attaining. The fires of greed, hatred, and delusion—toxic unconscious mental and emotional dispositions that cause people to harm themselves and one another and cause suffering— have been extinguished (nibbuta) in a person who attains nirvana.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are applicable to Jain doctrine?
1. The surest way of annihilating Karma is to practice penance.
2. Every object, even the smallest particle, has a soul.
3. Karma is the bane of the soul and must be ended.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Statement 1 is correct: According to Jain doctrine, the annihilation (nirjara) of karma comes about through penance, and the prevention (samvara) of the influx (asrava) and fixation (bandha) of karma in the soul is ensured by carefully disciplined conduct.\nStatement 2 is correct: Jiva or soul is a conscious substance. According to Jain doctrine, Souls are not only the property of animal and plant life, but also of entities such as stone, water and many other natural objects not looked upon as living by other sects.\nStatement 3 is correct: The Jain doctrine holds that every living and non-living being is gifted with souls. Each Jiva (soul) is eternally associated with Ajiva (non-sentient beings or non-conscious beings) because of karma. They are obstructed by karma, just as the natural light of the sun is hindered by clouds. By removing the karmas, a soul can remove bondage and regain its natural perfection.

questions.q:
With reference to the history of ancient India, which of the following was/were common to both Buddhism and Jainism?
1. Avoidance of extremities of penance and enjoyment
2. Indifference to the authority of the Vedas
3. Denial of efficacy of rituals
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Both opposed the ritualism and the sacrifices of Brahmanism and also challenged the supremacy of the Brahmanas. (Statement 3 is correct)\nBoth denied the authenticity of the Vedas as an infallible authority. (Statement 2 is correct)\nEven though both emphasised Ahimsa or non-violence, Jainism believes in extremities of penance, for example, the practice of Kaya klesh, a must for Jain monks who take the lifelong vow of diksha or monkhood, is excruciatingly painful. (Statement 1 is not correct)

questions.q: Lord Buddha's image is sometimes shown with the hand gesture called 'Bhumisparsha Mudra'. It symbolises:
options: Buddha's calling of the Earth to watch over Mara and to prevent Mara from disturbing his meditation.
Buddha's calling of the Earth to witness his purity and chastity despite the temptations of Mara.
Buddha's reminder to his followers that they all arise from the Earth and finally dissolve into the Earth, and thus this life is transitory.
Both the statements (a) and (b) are correct in this context
questions.explain: Bhumisparsha means touching the earth. It is most commonly known as the earth witness mudra. This mudra involves all the five fingers of the right hand extended to touch the ground. This posture of mudra symbolises the pose of Buddha at the time of enlightenment under the Bodhi tree, when he summoned the earth goddess Sthavara, to bear witness to his attainment of enlightenment. Shakyamuni Buddha is commonly represented upon his enlightenment throne with his right hand touching the earth and his left hand resting upon his lap in the gesture of meditation. This symbolises his method or skillful means in overcoming Mara (right hand), through the perfect wisdom of his deep meditation on emptiness (left hand).

questions.q:
With reference to the guilds (Shreni) of ancient India that played a very important role in the country's economy, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Every guild was registered with the central authority of the State and the king was the chief administrative authority on them.
2. The wages, rules of work, standards and prices were fixed by the guild.
3. The guild had judicial powers over its own members.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Ancient Indian guilds are a unique and multi-faceted form of organisation, which combined the functions of a democratic government, a trade union, a court of justice and a technological institution. The trained workers of the guilds provided a congenial atmosphere for work. Guilds were autonomous socio-economic entities, and Each guild had its own chief, assisted by others. The guilds regulated the wages, rules of work, standards, and prices, etc. The guilds had some judicial powers, some of them even had their own army and forces known as Screnibal.
